subject: RCA & staged remediation: transient node evaporation causing tenant cold-start amplification
messages:
From: Monitoring <alerts@redwood.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, oncall@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: [ALERT] dedicated-us-west-2 pool: rapid node disappearances detected

Alert summary:
- 09:11:42 PDT: 6/64 nodes in pool dedicated-us-west-2 marked unavailable in 2m window
- Affected tenants: multiple; increased cold-start latency observed for pinned tenants
- Symptoms: KV-cache reset, increased initialization p95 from 120ms -> 2.4s

Actions taken automatically: circuit opened for preemptible scheduling, synthetic throttling engaged.

--
This alert originated from the autoscaler health stream.
From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-21T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: [ALERT] dedicated-us-west-2 pool: rapid node disappearances detected

Team —
I pulled Artemis AI (host: artemis.ai) into the loop because they started seeing anomalous token latencies around the same time (reported via support). Short-term ask: can infra triage if this is instance-level preemptions or a control-plane propagation bug?

Initial notes from logs: several worker heartbeats dropped at 09:09:xx and a concurrent scheduler reschedule spike at 09:10:xx. I attached a small timeline.

Can someone own a customer-first reply? I can patch together the first notification.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Client Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference
From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@artemis.ai>
Cc: infra@artemis.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-21T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Interim update — dedicated-us-west-2 impact and next steps

Sarah —

Thanks for flagging the latency spike this morning. We detected a rapid series of node unregistrations in the dedicated-us-west-2 GPU pool starting at ~09:09 PDT that caused extra cold-starts for active tenants, and briefly increased p95 token latencies for a subset of your routes. Our on-call team has force-queued warmups and enabled aggressive prefix caching for affected routes to reduce the penalty.

What we know so far:
- Root symptom: a control-plane race during instance health reconciliation that resulted in ~10% of nodes being marked drained/evicted in a short window.
- Impact window: ~09:09–09:28 PDT. Most tenants saw degraded p95 for 6–12 minutes during reconciliation.
- Immediate mitigation: synthetic warmups and temporary burst allocation to Artemis tenant who reported highest impact.

What we are doing next:
- Engineering is collecting detailed heartbeats and kernel logs (ETA 2–3 hours).
- We will provide a full RCA and a staged remediation schedule by EOD.
- As a goodwill gesture we’ll apply a one-off credit covering 10% of affected minutes; will confirm amount once we finish the timeline.

Attachments: incident_timeline.csv (short), evap-log-snippet.txt

Sorry for the disruption — we know this is sensitive during your heavy training window. I’ll update you with the RCA and concrete customer-facing mitigations when available.

Best,
Tessa
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@artemis.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: infra@artemis.ai
Date: 2027-08-21T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Interim update — dedicated-us-west-2 impact and next steps

Thanks Tessa — appreciate the quick acknowledgement. A few asks from our side:
- Can you share the per-tenant p95/loss counts for 09:00–09:40? We need to map to our internal deploys.
- Please confirm the credit commitment and any follow-ups to avoid recurrence (we're sensitive to cold-start regressions).

We're standing by for a deeper RCA.

—Sarah
Head of ML Ops, Artemis AI
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-21T13:55:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Interim update — dedicated-us-west-2 impact and next steps

Quick internal summary for the customer-facing RCA:
- Root cause: a concurrency regression in the pool reconciliation code. Under a high-rate health-update scenario the reconciler could over-count transient failures and mark healthy nodes as drained if heartbeats crossed the resync boundary. This manifested as a short period where ~6–8 nodes were evacuated repeatedly (we're calling the phenomenon "evaporation").
- Contributing factor: our pre-warm heuristics weren't aggressive enough to absorb the sudden loss because the KV cache invalidated when pods re-anchored.
- Short-term mitigation implemented: revert the reconciliation window change (hotfix deployed at 11:40 PDT), force warmup allocations, and increase heartbeat tolerance.
- Next steps (detailed plan attached): code fix + improved simulation tests, rollout of staggered reconciliation, and a one-week observability dashboard for preemptive detection.

I will draft the RCA doc and the customer remediation schedule. Marissa, can you confirm the credit calc and attach the billing stub? Karthik, please prepare per-tenant impact stats for Artemis and include token-level p95 and cold-start counts.

Laura
VP, Platform Reliability
From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@artemis.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-22T18:45:00-07:00
Subject: Final RCA & staged remediation schedule — dedicated-us-west-2 (Aug 21)

Sarah —

Thank you for your patience. Attached is the final RCA and our staged remediation schedule (remediation_staged_plan_v1.pdf). TL;DR: the incident was caused by a reconciliation concurrency regression that could prematurely mark nodes as drained during a burst of health updates. We fixed and rolled back the problematic change, hardened heartbeat tolerance, and added simulation tests to catch the pattern.

Customer-facing summary:
- Impact window: 2027-08-21 09:09–09:28 PDT
- Scope: Artemis AI observed elevated p95 token latencies on three routes and an increased cold-start count for pinned sessions during the window.
- Remediation applied: hotfix rollback (11:40 PDT), forced warmups for affected tenants (11:45 PDT), monitoring rule for evaporation signature deployed (12:10 PDT).
- Preventative measures: staggered reconciliation rollout, KV-cache anchor improvements, and a one-week dashboard for preemptive alerts.
- Credit: pending final billing calc — Marissa will confirm but initial estimate is a credit of ~9.6% for the affected minutes tied to Artemis' committed capacity.

Next steps committed by Redwood:
- 48h: post-deploy soak + verification of the simulation harness
- 7 days: production metric dashboard and automatic alerting for evaporation patterns
- 30 days: full post-incident retrospective and code-level mitigation merged with QA sign-off

Attachments referenced: remediation_staged_plan_v1.pdf, incident_timeline.csv, evap-log-snippet.txt

If you'd like a live walkthrough of the RCA and the observability dashboard, we can schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow.

Apologies again — we're treating this as high priority.

Best regards,
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Client Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference

- incident_timeline.csv (rows: timestamp, event, node_id, tenant_id, p95_delta)
